# Bitcoin Runes Integration in Rosen Bridge
This document outlines the integration of Bitcoin Runes modules into the Rosen Bridge.
## Contents
- [Updates on Rosen Chains](#updates-on-rosen-chains)
- [Bitcoin Runes Integration](#bitcoin-runes-integration)
 - [Watcher Service](#watcher-service)
 - [Guard Service](#guard-service)
## Updates on Rosen Chains
[Rosen Chains](https://github.com/rosen-bridge/rosen-chains) is the primary dependency of the Guard service, where all chain-specific functions and behaviors are implemented. In the previous milestone, this module was integrated. However, during testing, several potential issues were identified, leading to a restructuring of the module to address them.
Runes protocol utilizes the `OP_RETURN` UTxOs on Bitcoin to write protocol data, such as transfer details. In the previous structure of Rosen Chains, every Rune in the input had to be specified during the transfer (using the `edict` field). However, the `OP_RETURN` UTxOs on Bitcoin have a soft limit of 80 bytes (i.e., transactions with `OP_RETURN` data exceeding 80 bytes will not be propagated by the nodes). Although having fewer Runes in inputs was aimed by the design, this was still a potential issue and impossible to avoid.
Another issue involved the first UTxO. Rosen sends user assets using the first box (or UTxO) in the transaction. On the other hand, the Runes protocol specifies that when spending a Runes UTxO, if no Runes protocol data is provided, all Runes are sent to the first non-`OP_RETURN` UTxO. To align with Runes specification, the change assets for Runes should ideally be in the first UTxO.
To address these issues, the structure was updated to follow these rules (specific to Bitcoin Runes):
- Each transaction should transfer only one Rune. For transferring multiple Runes, multiple transactions should be generated (the only exception is the Cold Storage type, which sends assets to the Cold address).
- UTxOs containing Runes should have the minimum UTxO v
